65:{"n":50,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"The chatbox appeared early, but the first request still waited for unused implementation modules. This keeps the required startup hooks and tool schemas, while reducing the code Node loads before dispatch.

- Share split Node bundles between the CLI and SDK. Load web, LSP, MCP, and subagent engines on demand.
- Cancel stale initialization and prevent old web results, curator callbacks, MCP connections, and LSP diagnostics from entering a replacement session.
- Check the built CLI with optional imports blocked, then exercise real first-turn tools. Verify public-name tarball installation and SDK class identity.

## Measurements

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

| First request | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh profile | 1988.8 / 2026.4 ms | 968.2 / 1007.0 ms |
| Repeated launch | 2597.6 / 2628.6 ms | 970.6 / 993.5 ms |

Median improvement is 51.3% fresh and 62.6% repeated. The complete default tool payload remains identical. These are controlled measurements, not a latency guarantee. First-use MCP status varied from about 126 ms to 3.1 seconds. Details and reproduction commands are in `packages/coding-agent/docs/interactive-startup.md`.

## Verification

- Rebased onto current master at v0.2.16. Five-package offline build passes without catalog regeneration.

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).

- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

65:{"n":50,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"The chatbox appeared early, but the first request still waited for unused implementation modules. This keeps the required startup hooks and tool schemas, while reducing the code Node loads before dispatch.

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

65:{"n":50,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"The chatbox appeared early, but the first request still waited for unused implementation modules. This keeps the required startup hooks and tool schemas, while reducing the code Node loads before dispatch.

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

### 50 perf: cut first-request startup latency by half 
 The chatbox appeared early, but the first request still waited for unused implementation modules. This keeps the required startup hooks and tool schemas, while reducing the code Node loads before dispatch.

- Share split Node bundles between the CLI and SDK. Load web, LSP, MCP, and subagent engines on demand.

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

No release, catalog regeneration, or installed-CLI changes.

 Codex OAuth sessions could compact too late during tool loops because lunR used optional maximum windows and only checked the threshold before a turn began. That could send an oversized follow-up request or trigger duplicate compaction errors.

This release uses each Codex route's advertised default window, checks compaction between complete tool-result batches, keeps tool call/result pairs intact, and makes repeated compaction harmless. It also defers the TUI history rebuild until the active turn settles.
